q1: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.st = f2.st
q2: SELECT a.drinker, b.drinker FROM Frequents AS a CROSS JOIN Frequents AS b WHERE a.drinker <> b.drinker AND a.bar = b.bar AND a.times_a_week = b.times_a_week

counterexample: INSERT INTO Drinker (name, address) VALUES ('A', '123 Main St'), ('B', '456 Elm St'); INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('The Bodega', '789 Oak St'); INSERT INTO Frequents (drinker, bar, times_a_week) VALUES ('A', 'The Bodega', 3), ('B', 'The Bodega', 3);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 selects pairs of drinkers who drink at the same bars the same number of times a week, while Q2 selects pairs of drinkers who drink at the same bars the same number of times a week and are not the same person.
counterexample_dsp: Create two drinkers, A and B, who drink at the same bar, The Bodega, 3 times a week.
